Reviewer_Question: Why these three architectures (ResNet18, DenseNet121, SwinUNETR)?
What_We_Know: ResNet18 tests transfer learning via MedicalNet pretraining; DenseNet121 tests dense convolutional feature reuse from scratch; SwinUNETR tests 3D windowed self-attention.
What_We_Infer: Pretrained CNNs learn compact feature spaces that resist majority loss collapse; transformers require stronger gradient signals.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Scratch-trained ResNet18 vs MedicalNet ResNet18 under identical cross-validation.

Reviewer_Question: Why 3D MRI rather than 2D slice classification?
What_We_Know: 3D MRI captures volumetric spatial context, infiltrative margins, and multi-parametric channel co-registration (FLAIR, T1w, T1gd, T2w).
What_We_Infer: Glioma grading requires 3D spatial assessment of heterogeneous necrotic cores and non-enhancing margins.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Direct comparison against 2D slice aggregation baseline.

Reviewer_Question: Why is severe class imbalance (19:1) important in this project?
What_We_Know: BraTS 2023 GLI cohort has 95.0% HGG and 5.0% LGG prevalence, matching clinical epidemiology.
What_We_Infer: Standard accuracy masks minority failure; unweighted empirical loss gradients are dominated by majority samples.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Synthetic oversampling (SMOTE 3D) vs dynamic modulating losses.

What_We_Know: Protocols B and C applied inverse-frequency and minority-boosted weights to counteract gradient imbalance.
What_We_Infer: Static weighting alters the loss landscape by scaling loss contributions inversely with frequency.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Multi-seed variance of class-weighted models under cross-validation.

Reviewer_Question: Why did class weighting produce different effects across architectures?
What_We_Know: CNN sensitivity declined (ResNet 75%->41.7%; DenseNet 66.7%->33.3%) while SwinUNETR sensitivity increased (0%->25%).
What_We_Infer: Static weighting over-penalizes majority gradients in structured CNN representations, but helps transformers escape majority plateaus.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Gradient norm tracking per layer during class-weighted training.

Reviewer_Question: Why did ResNet18 Protocol A receive additional cross-validation analysis?
What_We_Know: ResNet18 Protocol A achieved the highest locked-test Macro-F1 (0.8842) and LGG Recall (0.7500).
What_We_Infer: Top single-split performers warrant reliability auditing to detect potential partition sensitivity.

Reviewer_Question: Is the 75% locked-test LGG Recall reliable?
What_We_Know: 75% is verified on the locked test (9/12 LGG); 5-fold CV demonstrates an average of 50.55% +/- 32.74%.
What_We_Infer: The 75% result is an authentic upper-tier draw from a variable sensitivity distribution.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Repeated-seed test evaluation and pooled multi-split confidence intervals.

What_We_Know: Zero patient overlap; locked test was never passed to training dataloaders or early-stopping loops.
What_We_Infer: The locked-test evaluation is fully valid and uncontaminated.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: External validation on independent clinical hospital cohorts.

Reviewer_Question: Was the historical 0 -> 0.75 LGG Recall discrepancy caused by test leakage?
What_We_Know: Earlier 0.00 recall came from a 7-epoch checkpoint (restoring Ep 1); 0.75 recall came from a 25-epoch checkpoint (restoring Ep 19).
What_We_Infer: The difference stems from training optimization progression and checkpoint selection, not test leakage.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Epoch-by-epoch test probability logging under controlled multi-seed runs.

Reviewer_Question: Is the minority failure a representation problem or a decision-threshold problem?
What_We_Know: ROC-AUC is high (>= 0.86), but default tau = 0.50 yields conservative minority predictions.
What_We_Infer: Latent representation separates classes, but uncalibrated posterior probabilities cause threshold collapse.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Post-hoc probability calibration (Platt scaling / temperature scaling) vs loss-level modulation.

Reviewer_Question: Does threshold optimization solve the class imbalance problem?
What_We_Know: Validation tuning recovers sensitivity (e.g. SwinUNETR 0%->100%), but increases majority false positives.
What_We_Infer: Thresholding adjusts operating points along an invariant ROC curve; it does not expand discriminative capacity.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Cost-sensitive threshold selection under clinical utility functions.

Reviewer_Question: Why is Focal Loss the next logical experiment?
What_We_Know: Static class weighting failed to improve CNNs; fixed thresholds collapse under uncalibrated probabilities.
What_We_Infer: Focal Loss dynamically down-weights easy majority examples without distorting minority feature gradients.
What_We_Still_Need_to_Test: Empirical 5-fold cross-validation of Focal Loss across all 3 architectures.
